title: The zero scheme of a nonzero section of an invertible module on an integral scheme is an effective Cartier divisor
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and let $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$ with $s\neq0$. Let $Z(s)\subseteq X$ be the zero scheme of $s$ [def-pc-zero-scheme], with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_{Z(s)}\subseteq\mathcal O_X$. Then for every nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ on which $\mathcal L|_U$ is free on a generator $e$, writing $s|_U=a\,e$ with $a\in A$, the element $a$ is nonzero, hence a nonzerodivisor of the domain $A$, and $\mathcal I_{Z(s)}|_U$ is generated by $a$. In particular $\mathcal I_{Z(s)}$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], i.e. $Z(s)$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$ in the sense of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle].
